transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining. As you're all aware, we have an anonymous report alleging that a procurement vice president may have steered technology purchases toward a preferred supplier. Our preliminary review has examined the procurement policy, selected emails, and payment records, but reached no final conclusion. The audit committee expects my recommended resolution plan at this Friday's meeting. Before I can present anything, I need final sign-off from investigations, finance, employment, and insurance counsel — that's our standard practice. I'd like to use our time today to work through where each of you stands on this matter and what additional steps we need to take to get us to a defensible recommendation by Friday.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share an important update from the investigations side. After conducting two additional witness interviews this week, I've concluded that the procurement vice president did steer the purchases in violation of company policy. I have not yet finalized that conclusion in the preliminary review memorandum, but based on what I've gathered, the allegation is substantiated. I wanted to make sure everyone here has that information as we work toward Friday's recommendation.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Thank you, Thomas. That's significant. I also have an important update from the finance side. Yesterday, I completed a reconciliation of the supplier invoices against the approved purchase orders for the transactions under review. The reconciliation confirms that the company overpaid exactly $240,000 on those transactions. This finding was completed yesterday and is not yet included in the preliminary review packet. I think this is critical information for the audit committee recommendation, both in terms of quantifying the financial impact and informing any potential recovery or remediation steps.

transcript.text: I have an important update from the employment counsel side. In a confidential meeting this week, the reporting employee informed me that the vice president had begun excluding them from meetings after the report was made. This raises serious retaliation concerns. My required protective plan is anti-retaliation monitoring with check-ins every 14 days for exactly 60 days, but I have not yet added this to the investigation plan. I need to ensure this protective measure is incorporated before we present our recommendation to the audit committee on Friday.
